divergence_duo.accuracy: O(h) on a quasi-uniform icosahedral triangular mesh
divergence_duo.reference: Heikes et al. (2023), J. Adv. Model. Earth Syst. 15:e2022MS003192 (DUO icosahedral triangular C-grid); flux-form finite-volume divergence on the triangular PRIMAL cell, the icosahedral-triangular analogue of the MPAS Voronoi divergence (Skamarock et al. 2012, Mon. Wea. Rev. 140:3090-3105, Eq. 24) and the divergence_mpas template (esd-6g4.1). Discrete operator: (div F)_i = (1/A_i) * sum_{k=1}^{3} s_{i,k} * l_e * F_e, with e = edges_on_face[i,k] the k-th of the triangle's three primal edges, s_{i,k} = edge_sign_on_face[i,k] in {+1,-1} the outward-normal orientation (reference normal points from the lower-indexed to the higher-indexed of the edge's two incident faces; s = +1 when i is that lower-indexed face), l_e = dc_edge[e] the PRIMAL edge arc length (the shared triangle side the flux crosses; DUO's dc_edge is the cell-center analogue of MPAS's dv_edge, swapped because DUO cells are the triangular primal while MPAS cells are the Voronoi dual), A_i = tri_area[i] the spherical-triangle area (the Gauss-theorem area enclosed by the three primal edges — NOT the dc·dv diamond area_eff used by the nn_diffusion_duo Laplacian; area_eff leaves an O(1) consistency error here), and F_e the edge-normal flux. The coefficient s*l/A is build-time-constant grid geometry (const-folded); only F_e reaches the per-step hot tree. The reduction bound is the constant 3 (every closed-icosahedral triangle has exactly three real edges, no padding) — contrast divergence_mpas's index(n_edges_on_cell, i) for the 5/6-valent Voronoi dual.
